newsitem.title: MEXICO: Key files missing in case of Mexican drug lord.
newsitem.headline: Key files missing in case of Mexican drug lord.

text.p: Mexico's Attorney General's Office said on Tuesday it was investigating the theft of four volumes of the criminal files of notorious drug trafficker Juan Garcia Abrego.

Garcia Abrego, captured a year ago here in northern Nuevo Leon state, was extradited to the United States, where he was convicted in U.S. federal court on 22 counts of drug-trafficking, money-laundering and bribery. He is to be sentenced on Jan. 31.
Mexico, however, was building its own case against Garcia Abrego, a U.S. citizen who ran the enormous Gulf cartel in northeastern Mexico.
"The theft of the four volumes of the file in the case of Juan Garcia Abrego is being investigated," the Nuevo Leon delegation of the Attorney General's Office said in a statement.
During Garcia Abrego's trial in Houston, cartel insiders testified that Garcia Abrego paid off police and the deputy attorney general who was in charge of Mexico's anti-drug efforts at the time.

The Monterrey newspaper El Norte reported that the volumes and their only copies were stolen five months ago from the anti-drug office in Nuevo Leon, but it wasn't until nearly a week after the theft that authorities ordered an investigation.

At the time of his arrest, Garcia Abrego was on the FBI list of 10 most wanted criminals. Later, Mexican authorities confiscated 28 houses, two warehouses, 89 commerical lots and other properties allegedly belonging to Garcia Abrego.
A U.S. federal jury convicted him on Oct. 16
